_comment: The privacy notice and the website terms of the growth funnels, built into /g/uk-it-growth/privacy/ and /g/uk-it-growth/terms/ by scripts/build-g-growth.mjs. The text is the solicitor pack's draft (Claude Doc 'Solicitor pack (UK): commission, consent and three drafts'), with the open brackets closed as described in LAUNCH.md, section 13. Block types: h2, p, ul, table (head + rows), button. Links: [[label|/path]] or [[label|@privacy]] / [[label|@terms]]; {EMAIL} becomes the contact address as a link. A block, or a table row written as {"when": ..., "cells": [...]}, is kept only if its condition holds: "register" is config.json legal.registerCheck (true only while COMPANIES_HOUSE_API_KEY is set in production), "unless": "register" marks a block or row kept only while no check is made. The daily check (netlify/functions/lead-reconcile) reports the flag and the key disagreeing. Change the date in 'updated' whenever the words change. No dashes, no exclamation marks, no rate near the word commission: the build refuses them.

blocks.p: This notice explains how Elevate Marketing uses personal data on its campaign pages for UK IT services firms, private healthcare providers and law firms, in the application and booking steps that follow them, and on its older enquiry page. The main website at getelevateleads.com has its own privacy policy.

Elevate Marketing is a trading name of EngeCo AS, a Norwegian company (organisation no. 924 490 926) at Midtfjellet 66, 5363 Ågotnes, Norway. EngeCo AS decides how your details are used. In data protection law that makes us the controller. You can reach us at {EMAIL}.

blocks.p: We use your answers to decide automatically which page you see next: a booking page, a page saying that we will review your application, a page saying that we will ask again later, or a page saying that we cannot help at the moment. A person checks every application sent for review. A person may also read the applications on the last of these pages, to see whether another service of ours could help, but we contact you about that only if you press the button on that page. If you think we got it wrong, email us and we will look again.

blocks.p: To ask, write to {EMAIL}. We answer within one month. If a request is complicated, the law lets us take longer, and we will tell you why. We may need to check who you are first. We do not charge for this, except in the narrow cases the law allows.

If you think we have handled your details wrongly, please tell us first so that we can put it right. You can also complain to the regulator. In the UK that is the Information Commissioner's Office (ico.org.uk). In Norway, where we are based, it is Datatilsynet (datatilsynet.no).

blocks.h2: 9. Meta and the measurement of our advertising

blocks.p: If you choose Accept, two things happen. The Meta pixel on our pages tells Meta which pages you saw. And when your application is one we take forward, our server sends Meta a short message so that Meta can match it to the advertisement you clicked. That message holds scrambled (hashed) versions of your email address, first name and last name, your IP address, your browser details, and the identifiers Meta set when you clicked. We send no phone number. We use this only to see which advertisements lead to real applications, and to improve who sees our advertising.
If you choose Decline, none of this is sent, and we do not keep the advertising identifiers with your application.
What Meta does when it shows you our advertisement is covered by Meta's own privacy policy. Meta also decides for itself how it uses some of what it receives.
